hold_text: This PR adds a FOURTH actor to the landing route — a cadence job that pushes merge commits to `automation/*` branches which already have auto-merge ARMED, and re-asserts their R13 merge-slot claims. By R12 it must not land itself: the change and its own approval would be the same act, and a mistake in it disarms the very check that would have caught the mistake. It is registered in this guard's own LANDING_MACHINERY in the same commit, for exactly the reason MI-208 registered `.github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml` there — a mistake in it LANDS a pull request rather than merely failing to — so R8 verifies this hold against the diff rather than taking it on trust. WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD READ ONCE, in three parts. (1) THE SWEEPER REFRESHES AND NEVER CLOSES, and only ever refreshes a PR it has shown carries content `main` lacks that nothing newer supersedes. That is not caution for its own sake: every one of these PRs already has auto-merge armed, so refreshing one is not 'letting it be judged again', it is LANDING it on green, and refreshing a PR whose register is OLDER than main's would REWIND main — worse than the strand it fixes. (2) IT PUSHES WITH `BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN`, NOT `GITHUB_TOKEN`: a GITHUB_TOKEN push creates no workflow runs, so the refresh would mint a head sha nothing grades, turning 'stranded with stale red checks' into 'stranded with no checks at all' — which reads as progress. (3) AN UNREADABLE OPEN-PR LIST EXITS 2 as COULD NOT LOOK and is never reported as an empty queue. ⚠️ THIS PARAGRAPH SAID 'DEPLOYED, NOT OBSERVED … NO BRANCH HAS BEEN PUSHED BY IT'. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE AND IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING — it would have had you approve believing the refresh path was unexercised. OBSERVED, three times, all by HAND-RUNNING the script (the workflow is not on `main`, so it has no cron and the MECHANISM is still unproven — the SCRIPT is what is proven). #11543 and #11490 were refreshed and merged; #11557 was refreshed from a genuinely conflicted start and merged as f058af3a, landing the digest receipt that would otherwise have red-lined `main` repo-wide at 17:39Z. Each was verified as EFFECT and never from the sweeper's report: merge-base equal to main's tip, the slot file present in the branch's own diff, the claim naming that branch, and `check_pr_landing.py` passing in a worktree checked out UNDER THE REAL BRANCH NAME. ⚠️ AND THE FIRST LIVE RUN CARRIED A FALSE SUCCESS, which is the single most important thing to read here: `refresh()` used `git commit --no-edit`, which no-ops on the no-conflict path because `git merge` has already committed; the exit code was discarded and the function reported 'refreshed and pushed' for a claim it never wrote. Fixed with an explicit `-m`, an exit-code check, a tree reset, and effect-verification against the merge-base before the push — three tests, mutation-checked. ⚠️ TWO FURTHER DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY HAND-TRIAGING THE LIVE QUEUE AND ARE FIXED HERE. (i) `APPEND_ONLY` was a hardcoded path list holding ONE entry while the queue held TWO append-only classes; #11475 carries `comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl` = main + 427 rows main lacks. It graded safely only BY ACCIDENT (JSONL does not parse as a JSON object), and stamping `generated_at` — the remedy this PR itself files for the 13 undated PRs — would have ARMED the row-dropping bug. Append is now detected as a PROPERTY (a strict byte-prefix), and a payload absent from main gets its own state, `absent_on_main`, because `dated_at` returns None for two different reasons. EIGHT states now, not seven. (ii) `carries_append_only` was blocking the REFRESH as well as the close — and ALL TEN open work-digest PRs grade that way, because a digest always queues a ping row, so the sweeper could NEVER refresh the carrier of `check_digest_liveness`, the TIGHTEST repo-wide clock. It is now an annotation applied after the register verdict and exempt on refresh; it still can never make a PR actionable. 21 tests, not 11. ⚠️ AND ONE MODE THIS FIX DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than hidden: when the producing run hits the GitHub API rate limit, `gh pr create` fails and the branch is pushed with NO PR AT ALL (measured on run 34355107317). The sweeper enumerates OPEN PRS, so such a branch is invisible to it — the premise is right and the INPUT SET is wrong; it should iterate branches. Recorded on the WO and deliberately NOT rushed into this PR, because it changes what the sweeper may act on.
why: Fixes the CLASS behind WO-20260909-EVERY-PR-IN-THE-REPO-IS-RED. MEASURED 2026-09-09, population = all 52 open PRs: 50 have `automation/*` head refs and 47 of those carry no R13 merge-slot claim, having been cut before MI-208/#11494 landed at 06:37:54Z. The cut is exact — #11493 (opened 06:00:16Z) has none, #11499 (06:38:14Z, twenty seconds later) has one — which confirms #11494 works and identifies the 47 as pre-fix strands rather than 47 bugs. THE CLASS: `.github/actions/commit-to-main` already does everything a producer can do for its own PR — all 25 of 25 call sites set `verify-merged: true` (verified by parsing every workflow that references the action; an earlier grep-based count of 7 was a `-A12` window artefact and is retracted), and `refresh-stale-branch` demonstrably works, since #11499's head is a 'Merge main so the required checks re-run against the current base' commit. But all of it lives inside the PRODUCING RUN'S OWN LIFETIME: one `verify-timeout-minutes` window (default 30), one refresh attempt. When the job exits the branch has NO OWNER, so any blocker outliving that window strands it permanently while the producer's next cron opens another that strands identically. THE WO ASKED WHICH OF THREE IT IS. It is (a), but the fix cannot live where (a) implies — not in the producing workflow, because that run is over; it must be a cadence job that outlives it. (b) is REFUSED as not implementable: `main` is branch-protected and rejects a direct workflow push (GH006), which is the documented reason `commit-to-main` exists at all, so 'land receipts directly' means removing branch protection from the path that writes to main most often — an unguarded lane. (c) is REFUSED as wrong on purpose: a time-based guard reading the freshest receipt across OPEN PRs would grade an unlanded receipt as if it had landed, so a watcher whose output can never merge would read `fresh` forever — the guard going quiet in exactly the state it exists to announce — and it would make a required check depend on live API state, so the same commit grades differently on re-run. THE NULL IS REFUSED TOO, with evidence: the receipts SHOULD keep gating every PR, because the guard did its job — it went red at 07:44:31Z and the condition was visible repo-wide within minutes. What failed is that the REMEDY path is not as automatic as the alarm. Adds `scripts/ops/sweep_stale_automation_prs.py` (seven states, never collapsed; only `refresh` is actionable and a test pins that), `.github/workflows/stale-automation-sweep.yml` (2h — CHOSEN off the TIGHTEST of the four repo-wide receipt-guard windows, `check_digest_liveness` at 6h, not off queue volume), 11 tests, a catalog row, and the LANDING_MACHINERY registration above. ⚠️ THE SAFETY PROPERTY IS THAT IT NEVER CLOSES, and the reason is measured: a first pass at this triage classified by the newest dated register alone and called 22 PRs cleanly superseded when the true figure was 15 — SEVEN work-digest PRs each carried a `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` row absent from main, so auto-closing would have silently dropped seven operator notifications, the hazard `OPEN-PRS.json`'s #10902/#10908/#10914 rows already record. That correction is planted as a test rather than only described. Touches no src/, config/, deploy/ or order path.
